clue.text: Canal-vessel a morning before

indicators.note: the morning abbreviation is placed ahead of the letter A in the answer

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
AM (ante meridiem) is the abbreviation for morning

explanation.surface: A list describing a boat on a canal one early morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' says the morning abbreviation comes ahead of 'a', so the order is PAN, AM, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama is the famous ship canal linking the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: Billy the Kid?

parts.note: a billy is a male goat and a kid is a young one, so the kid is the billy's kin; the hide of a goat is also kid leather

explanation.surface: A one-line reference to the American outlaw Billy the Kid.
explanation.walkthrough: The outlaw's name is read as farmyard family: a kid is the billy goat's kin, and kid is also leather made from goat hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather is made from the hide of young goats, so it is a goat's hide.

clue.text: Showing ill-will often as a deficit opens up

indicators.note: something that opens up is spread out into a new shape, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sours whenever a shortfall in the accounts appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens up' rearranges the fifteen letters of OFTEN AS A DEFICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking affection or showing hostility is displaying bad feeling towards someone.

clue.text: Small deposit of building society?

parts.note: a building society is a British savings bank, but here it is a colony of insects that build, and their small deposit is the mound of earth they pile up

explanation.surface: A modest sum lodged with a British savings bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A building society is a British mutual savings and mortgage lender; read literally it is a society of builders, the insect colony, whose deposit is a heap of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants excavate soil and heap it in a little mound over their nest.

clue.text: The very thing for Tom's kitchen-tools!

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something excellent, just what is wanted
Tom is a male cat, and whiskers are read as things that whisk, kitchen utensils

explanation.surface: Praise for the perfect gift of utensils for someone called Tom's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a tomcat; its whiskers are recast as whisks, the kitchen tools that beat eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises something as excellent, the best possible; a tomcat's whiskers belong to the feline.

clue.text: Arrived with constable, say, in judge's chamber

parts.note: came means arrived
the painter John Constable was an RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A police constable arrives at a judge's private room.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is the painter, not a police officer: he was a member of the Royal Academy, so an RA. 'In camera' means in a judge's private room.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera is Latin for room; a hearing held in a judge's private room is said to be 'in camera'.

clue.text: Boss of horse-breeding establishment -

definitions.meaning: a boss is a raised knob or round metal ornament
a farm where stallions are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: The manager in charge of a horse-breeding farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like the person in charge but means a raised knob, like a decorative stud on leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative raised knob is a boss; a stable of breeding horses is a stud farm.

clue.text: Reverse gas-ring for this pudding

indicators.note: the instruction to turn round applies to the word gas, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Turn back the cooker's gas ring to make this dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' applies only to the gas, not the ring; a gas ring is a hob burner, but here the ring is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk pudding is made from the starchy granules of sago palm pith.

clue.text: Tavern which has a socially acceptable name

parts.note: in means fashionable, socially accepted

explanation.surface: A pub with a respectable-sounding name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is a pub, a public house offering drink and lodging.

clue.text: Dickens of a site for cricket!

definitions.text: Dickens of a site for cricket!

parts.words: Dickens of a site for cricket!
parts.note: refers to Charles Dickens's Christmas story The Cricket on the ..., where the insect sits by the fireside; 'a dickens of' also means a tremendous

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a tremendous cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the chirping insect, not the British bat-and-ball game; Dickens wrote a Christmas book about one that lives beside the fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireplace floor, where the insect sits in the Dickens title, is the domestic fire's spot.

clue.text: Sacred word that could catch a trespasser, almost?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the device is dropped

parts.note: a mantrap is a device set to catch trespassers

explanation.surface: A holy word that might stop an intruder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter P from MANTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or syllable chanted in Hindu or Buddhist meditation.

clue.text: Had a nice break in Spanish estate?

indicators.note: breaking the words lets their letters be put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed a holiday at a Spanish country property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a holiday but signals that HAD A NICE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large ranch or landed estate in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Polytechnic standard raised? .

parts.note: poly-technic is read as many skills, and a standard, or flag, that is raised on a ship is a jack, so the flag of a person of many crafts

explanation.surface: A question about academic levels improving at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a British college; read as Greek it means 'many arts', and a jack is a flag, a standard that is hoisted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person who can turn their hand to many kinds of work.

clue.text: Dead-letter found in Market Harborough

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the town name, spanning the join of its two words

explanation.surface: An undeliverable letter turns up in a Leicestershire market town.
explanation.walkthrough: A dead letter is usually undeliverable post; here it is a letter of an alphabet no longer used. Market Harborough is a town in Leicestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is an Old English letter that has fallen out of use in modern English spelling.

clue.text: Main tender left from highest point

indicators.note: from says the left abbreviation is taken away out of the peak word

parts.note: a pinnacle is a peak or highest point

explanation.surface: An offer made earnestly by someone who has come down from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, and a tender is a boat serving a ship, so 'Main tender' is a ship's boat, not a chief bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship, a ship's boat at sea.

clue.text: Artificial language spoken at wedding ceremonies?

definitions.meaning: a constructed international language devised in 1907 as a reform of Esperanto
the words of consent each partner says when taking their vows

explanation.surface: A question about which invented tongue is used when couples marry.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I DO, the second sense is the vow said at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an invented auxiliary language derived from Esperanto; the two-word vow is the bride's and groom's assent.

clue.text: Bashful about skin-blemish that is blackish

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shy word wraps the blemish

parts.note: shy means bashful
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A timid person fussing over a dark spot on their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark complexion, darkish in colour.

clue.text: It takes a turn for the better

definitions.text: It takes a turn for the better

parts.words: It takes a turn for the better
parts.note: for the better is read as for the person who bets, and the turn is a spin of a wheel in a casino game

explanation.surface: Something that improves matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the better' is read as 'for the bettor', the gambler, whose stake rides on the spinning wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game in which bettors wager on where a ball lands on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Upside down ..like the Ancient Mariner, for instance!

definitions.meaning: turned the other way round, opposite

definitions.text: like the Ancient Mariner, for instance
definitions.meaning: Coleridge's The Rime of the Ancient Mariner is a poem, so it is written in poetic lines

explanation.surface: A remark that something is topsy-turvy, like Coleridge's old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN VERSE, the second sense says the Rime of the Ancient Mariner is a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means opposite or turned over; a poem such as Coleridge's is written in metrical lines.

clue.text: Yes, count silicon-chips in a painstaking way

indicators.note: chipping breaks something into bits, so the letters of these words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Agreeing to count computer chips very carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' looks like silicon chips but signals that YES COUNT SILICON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something conscientiously means doing it diligently and with great care.

clue.text: Round rail's damaged — tar needed

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of order, so these are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
the letters of rail's, with its S

explanation.surface: A damaged rail needs tar to mend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges O and RAILS. 'Tar' is the old word for a seaman, not road tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar is a crossword-favourite word for a seaman.

clue.text: General method for lateral drift

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A general's approach to dealing with sideways drift.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is the sideways movement of a ship blown downwind off its course.

clue.text: Flouting of French betrothed

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiance is a man who is betrothed

explanation.surface: A French engaged couple defying convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Flouting authority is open disobedience, contemptuous resistance.

clue.text: Translation of dead Scandinavian books

indicators.note: translating changes one form into another, so the letters of the next word are reordered

explanation.surface: Rendering ancient Norse texts from a language nobody speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' rearranges DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are two Old Norse collections of poetry and mythology from Iceland.

clue.text: Zoo-man behind the strikers?

definitions.meaning: a person who looks after animals in a zoo
in cricket the gloved fielder crouches behind the batsmen, who strike the ball

explanation.surface: A zoo worker standing behind protesting workers on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The strikers are cricket batsmen, not industrial strikers; in cricket the fielder who crouches behind the batsman is the wicket-keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant who cares for zoo animals; in cricket, the fielder stationed behind the batting player.

clue.text: It follows road-repairs will be skilful

indicators.note: follows means the word it comes after the rearranged road letters
repairs as road works suggests the letters of the street word are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Road repairs will need a deft touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road-repairs' looks like roadworks; the hyphen hides that 'repairs' is the signal to rearrange, and 'follows' puts 'It' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means dexterous, clever with the hands or mind.

clue.text: Title 'of man serving in Rugby, initially?

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: How a schoolmaster at Rugby School is addressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English public school, where pupils call a master by this title, so the surface supports the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title given to a knight or baronet and a form of respectful address.

clue.text: Role-reversal can let an actor down

indicators.note: reversal means the role word is read from back to front

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A badly reversed role can disappoint a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let an actor down' means drop them through the stage floor, via a trapdoor, not disappoint them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage trapdoor lowers a performer out of sight beneath the boards.
